userMessage: Build an ESP32-based vibration monitor using an MPU6050. It should stream acceleration telemetry and analyze stationary sensor noise to verify that accel_x RMS noise stays below 0.10 g.

generate-project-brief.goal: Design and prototype an ESP32-based vibration monitor that continuously streams acceleration telemetry from an MPU6050 inertial sensor and verifies that the stationary accel_x RMS noise level remains below 0.10 g.
generate-project-brief.problemStatement: Vibration monitoring applications require reliable, low-noise inertial sensing combined with real-time telemetry. Without a verified noise floor, acceleration data cannot be trusted to distinguish true vibration events from sensor artifact. This project must establish that the accel_x channel's stationary RMS noise stays below 0.10 g while simultaneously streaming live acceleration data from an ESP32 and MPU6050 combination.
generate-project-brief.intendedContext: Early-stage embedded prototype intended for vibration sensing and monitoring use cases. The device is microcontroller-based, uses a fixed MCU (ESP32) and a fixed inertial sensor (MPU6050) as stated constraints, and is at the concept stage with no existing implementation to modify or debug.
scope: Interface the ESP32 with the MPU6050 inertial sensor to acquire raw acceleration data.
Stream acceleration telemetry from the ESP32 to an external destination.
Implement stationary noise analysis to compute the RMS value of the accel_x channel.
Enforce a pass/fail verification that accel_x RMS noise remains below the 0.10 g threshold.
Define the data acquisition pipeline including sampling, buffering, and transmission of acceleration samples.
outOfScope: PCB layout, schematic design, or hardware validation of an existing circuit.
Firmware debugging or diagnosis of an already-implemented system.
Detailed component selection beyond the user-stated ESP32 and MPU6050 constraints.
Deployment, purchasing, or production readiness activities.
Gyroscope channel processing (unless later confirmed in scope by the user).
Enclosure design or mechanical mounting engineering.
successCriteria: The accel_x channel RMS noise, measured under stationary conditions, is verified to be below 0.10 g.
Acceleration telemetry is streamed continuously from the ESP32 to an external destination without data loss under normal operating conditions.
The noise verification procedure produces a clear pass or fail indication against the 0.10 g threshold.
The system correctly acquires and processes acceleration data from the MPU6050 at a defined sampling rate.
The prototype operates stably for a representative monitoring session without requiring manual intervention.

assumptions.statement: The microcontroller is an ESP32, as explicitly stated by the user.
The inertial sensor is an MPU6050, as explicitly stated by the user.

The project is at the concept stage and no existing implementation exists to be modified or debugged.
A single prototype unit is the target deliverable for this stage, not a production run.

requirements.statement: The device shall use an ESP32 as its microcontroller.
requirements.rationale: The user explicitly stated the ESP32 as the microcontroller constraint.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspection of hardware design and firmware build configuration confirming ESP32 is the host MCU.
acceptanceCriteria: The hardware design identifies an ESP32 as the microcontroller.
Firmware is compiled and linked for the ESP32 target.

requirements.statement: The device shall use an MPU6050 as its inertial measurement sensor.
requirements.rationale: The user explicitly stated the MPU6050 as the inertial sensor constraint.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspection of hardware design and firmware driver confirming MPU6050 is the connected inertial sensor.
acceptanceCriteria: The hardware design identifies an MPU6050 as the inertial sensor.
Firmware successfully initializes and communicates with the MPU6050.

requirements.statement: The device shall continuously acquire acceleration data from the inertial sensor and stream it as telemetry to an external destination.
requirements.rationale: The user explicitly required streaming of acceleration telemetry.
requirements.verificationMethod: Functional test: observe that acceleration data packets are transmitted to the external destination at a regular cadence during device operation.
acceptanceCriteria: Acceleration data is transmitted continuously without manual intervention.
A receiving host or endpoint can decode and display the streamed acceleration values.
No data gaps exceeding a defined timeout occur during normal operation.

requirements.statement: The device shall perform a stationary sensor noise analysis on the accel_x channel and verify that its RMS noise value remains below 0.10 g.
requirements.rationale: The user explicitly required noise analysis and a specific accel_x RMS noise threshold of 0.10 g.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test: place the device on a stable, vibration-free surface; collect a stationary accel_x sample window; compute RMS noise; confirm the result is less than 0.10 g.
acceptanceCriteria: The device computes RMS noise over a defined stationary sample window for the accel_x channel.
The computed RMS noise value is less than 0.10 g.
The device reports a pass/fail result for the noise verification check.

requirements.statement: The device shall report the outcome of the accel_x RMS noise verification (pass or fail) in a manner observable by the operator or receiving system.
requirements.rationale: A noise verification step is only useful if its result is communicated; this follows necessarily from the requirement to verify noise.
requirements.verificationMethod: Functional test: trigger a noise verification run and confirm that a clear pass/fail indication is produced (e.g., via telemetry message, status output, or local indicator).
acceptanceCriteria: A pass result is indicated when accel_x RMS noise is below 0.10 g.
A fail result is indicated when accel_x RMS noise meets or exceeds 0.10 g.
The indication is observable without requiring access to internal firmware state.

requirements.statement: The telemetry stream shall include a timestamp or sequence identifier with each acceleration data record to allow ordering and latency assessment at the receiving end.
requirements.rationale: Telemetry streams for vibration monitoring typically require temporal context to be useful; without timestamps or sequence numbers, data ordering and gap detection are not possible.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspection of telemetry packet format and functional test confirming each record carries a timestamp or sequence number.
acceptanceCriteria: Each transmitted acceleration record contains a timestamp or monotonically increasing sequence number.
The receiving system can reconstruct the order of samples from the identifiers alone.

requirements.statement: The device shall acquire acceleration samples at a defined, consistent sampling rate sufficient to characterize the vibration frequencies of interest.
requirements.rationale: A consistent sampling rate is a prerequisite for meaningful RMS noise computation and vibration frequency analysis; the specific rate has not been defined by the user and must be confirmed.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test: log sample timestamps over a defined interval and verify that the inter-sample period is consistent and matches the configured rate within an acceptable tolerance.
acceptanceCriteria: The sampling rate is configurable or fixed at a documented value.
Inter-sample jitter does not exceed ±5% of the nominal sample period.
The sampling rate satisfies the Nyquist criterion for the highest vibration frequency of interest.

requirements.statement: The noise analysis shall be computed over a sample window of sufficient length to produce a statistically stable RMS estimate.
requirements.rationale: RMS noise computed over too few samples is statistically unreliable; a minimum window length is necessary for the verification to be meaningful, but the specific value has not been stated by the user.
requirements.verificationMethod: Analysis: demonstrate that the RMS estimate converges (varies by less than a defined tolerance) as sample count increases; confirm the chosen window meets this criterion.
acceptanceCriteria: The sample window length used for RMS computation is documented.
Repeated noise verification runs on a stationary device produce RMS values that agree within ±0.005 g.

requirements.statement: The device shall maintain a reliable communication link to the telemetry destination such that no more than a defined percentage of acceleration data records are lost under normal operating conditions.
requirements.rationale: Telemetry reliability is a standard performance concern for streaming sensor devices; the acceptable loss rate has not been specified by the user.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test: transmit a known number of sequenced records and count missing sequence numbers at the receiver; confirm loss rate is within the defined threshold.
acceptanceCriteria: Data loss rate does not exceed the defined threshold under normal operating conditions.
Lost records are detectable via sequence number gaps at the receiver.

requirements.statement: The device shall be powered by a supply appropriate for its deployment context, and shall operate correctly across the full range of that supply's voltage variation.
requirements.rationale: Every embedded device requires a defined power source; the user has not specified whether the device is mains-powered, battery-powered, or USB-powered, nor any power budget.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test: operate the device at the minimum and maximum expected supply voltages and confirm correct functional behavior throughout.
acceptanceCriteria: The power source type and voltage range are documented.
The device operates correctly at the minimum specified supply voltage.
The device operates correctly at the maximum specified supply voltage.

requirements.statement: The device shall operate within a defined ambient temperature range without degradation of measurement accuracy or communication reliability.
requirements.rationale: Operating environment has not been specified; a temperature range is required to validate component selection and system reliability.
requirements.verificationMethod: Test or analysis: verify device operation at the boundary temperatures of the defined range and confirm acceleration measurement accuracy and telemetry link remain within specification.
acceptanceCriteria: The operating temperature range is documented.
Acceleration measurement accuracy is maintained across the full temperature range.
Telemetry communication remains functional across the full temperature range.

requirements.statement: The device firmware shall be structured such that the noise verification function and the telemetry streaming function can be independently tested.
requirements.rationale: Nexus workflow policy requires that requirements be verifiable; independent testability of the two primary functions supports this.
requirements.verificationMethod: Inspection of firmware architecture and demonstration that each function can be exercised in isolation during testing.
acceptanceCriteria: A test procedure exists for noise verification that does not require an active telemetry link.
A test procedure exists for telemetry streaming that does not require a noise verification run.

generate-requirements.requirementSummary: Twelve requirements have been derived for the ESP32-based vibration monitor. Two hardware constraints (ESP32 MCU, MPU6050 sensor) are confirmed user-explicit. Two core functional requirements — continuous acceleration telemetry streaming and accel_x RMS noise verification below 0.10 g — are confirmed from explicit user statements. A further user-implied requirement captures the need to report the noise verification outcome. Seven system-inferred and project-policy requirements address telemetry timestamping, sampling rate consistency, noise window adequacy, telemetry reliability, power supply, operating temperature, and firmware testability; all are marked needs-confirmation or proposed and require user input to be fully specified. Seven dimensions remain unresolved and are listed in missingDimensions.

generate-functional-architecture.systemBoundary: The system boundary encompasses all functional subsystems resident on the ESP32-based vibration monitor device, from raw inertial data acquisition through processing, noise verification, and telemetry output. External to the boundary are: the physical environment being monitored, the telemetry sink/host receiving streamed data, and any external power supply. The MPU6050 inertial measurement unit is a user-stated hardware constraint and is represented as the sensing node at the system boundary.

nodes.name: Inertial Sensing Unit
responsibilities: Acquire raw acceleration samples from the MPU6050 (user-stated constraint) on all active axes at a configured sampling rate.
Acquire raw gyroscope samples if gyroscope channels are determined to be in scope.
Present digitized inertial data to the acquisition interface for retrieval by the processing subsystem.
Maintain sensor configuration state (full-scale range, digital low-pass filter settings, output data rate).

nodes.name: Sensor Acquisition Interface
responsibilities: Poll or interrupt-drive the inertial sensing unit to retrieve raw acceleration (and optionally gyroscope) samples at the required rate.
Convert raw digital counts to physical units (g for acceleration) using the configured full-scale range.
Buffer incoming samples and pass them to the signal processing subsystem.
Detect and report sensor communication faults or data-ready timeouts.

nodes.name: Signal Processing Engine
responsibilities: Receive calibrated acceleration sample streams from the acquisition interface.
Apply any required digital filtering (e.g., windowing, anti-alias) to the sample stream.
Compute time-domain and frequency-domain features from the acceleration data as needed for vibration characterization.
Prepare processed acceleration frames for both telemetry output and noise analysis.
Partition data into stationary-condition windows for noise analysis when triggered.

nodes.name: Noise Verification Subsystem
responsibilities: Receive stationary-condition acceleration windows from the signal processing engine.
Compute the RMS value of accel_x samples over each analysis window.
Compare computed accel_x RMS against the 0.10 g threshold.
Emit a pass/fail noise verification result and the measured RMS value.
Determine and enforce the stationary-condition detection criterion (e.g., low variance gate) to ensure analysis windows are valid.
Support both one-time calibration-mode and continuous runtime-check modes (mode selection is an unresolved decision).

nodes.name: Data Buffer and Storage
responsibilities: Maintain ring buffers or FIFO queues for raw and processed acceleration samples to decouple acquisition rate from telemetry transmission rate.
Store noise verification results and associated timestamps for retrieval by the telemetry subsystem.
Optionally persist telemetry frames locally if the transport link is unavailable (store-and-forward capability; scope is an unresolved decision).
Manage buffer overflow conditions and report them to the control subsystem.

nodes.name: System Control and Scheduling
responsibilities: Orchestrate the operational state machine: initialization, normal streaming, noise-verification, fault, and low-power states.
Schedule acquisition, processing, noise analysis, and telemetry tasks to meet timing requirements.
Receive and apply configuration parameters (sampling rate, noise-check mode, threshold overrides) from the user-interface or telemetry subsystem.
Propagate fault and status events between subsystems.
Enforce the ESP32 (user-stated constraint) resource allocation across concurrent functional tasks.

nodes.name: Telemetry and Communication Subsystem
responsibilities: Retrieve processed acceleration frames and noise verification results from the data buffer.
Serialize data into a structured telemetry format suitable for the chosen transport (transport type is an unresolved decision).
Transmit telemetry frames to the external host or sink over the selected interface.
Receive inbound configuration or command messages from the external host and forward them to the control subsystem.
Monitor link health and report connectivity status to the control subsystem.
Leverage the ESP32's (user-stated constraint) integrated wireless or wired communication capability for transport.

nodes.name: Local Status and Diagnostic Interface
responsibilities: Present real-time system status, noise verification pass/fail results, and fault indicators via local output means (e.g., indicator signals, display, or serial diagnostic port — form factor is an unresolved decision).
Accept local user inputs for triggering noise verification runs or resetting fault states.
Expose diagnostic information to aid in field verification of the 0.10 g noise threshold compliance.

nodes.name: Power Management Subsystem
responsibilities: Regulate and distribute power to all active subsystems from the external supply source.
Implement power-mode transitions (active, reduced-rate, sleep) under direction of the control subsystem to manage energy consumption.
Monitor supply voltage and report under-voltage conditions to the control subsystem.
Ensure the MPU6050 (user-stated constraint) and ESP32 (user-stated constraint) receive stable supply voltages within their specified operating ranges.

edges.description: Raw digitized acceleration (and optionally gyroscope) samples transferred from the MPU6050 inertial sensing unit to the acquisition interface at the configured output data rate.
Calibrated, unit-converted acceleration samples (in g) passed from the acquisition interface to the signal processing engine for filtering and feature extraction.
Processed acceleration frames and derived features written to the data buffer for decoupled consumption by the telemetry and noise verification subsystems.
Stationary-condition acceleration windows (accel_x and other active axes) forwarded from the signal processing engine to the noise verification subsystem for RMS computation.
Noise verification results (measured accel_x RMS value, pass/fail status, timestamp) written to the data buffer for inclusion in telemetry and local display.
Buffered telemetry frames (processed acceleration data and noise verification results) read by the telemetry subsystem for serialization and transmission.
Inbound configuration commands and operational directives received from the external host, forwarded to the system control subsystem for application.
Sampling rate, active-axis selection, and start/stop acquisition commands issued by the control subsystem to the acquisition interface.
Filter configuration, windowing parameters, and processing mode directives issued by the control subsystem to the signal processing engine.
Noise-check mode selection (one-time calibration vs. continuous runtime), threshold override, and trigger commands issued by the control subsystem to the noise verification subsystem.
Telemetry enable/disable, transmission rate, and link management directives issued by the control subsystem to the telemetry subsystem.
Power-mode transition requests (active, reduced-rate, sleep) issued by the control subsystem to the power management subsystem.
Noise verification pass/fail result and measured accel_x RMS value sent to the local status interface for immediate user-visible indication.
Local user inputs (e.g., trigger noise verification, reset faults) captured by the local status interface and forwarded to the control subsystem.
Regulated supply voltage delivered to the MPU6050 inertial sensing unit.
Regulated supply voltage delivered to the sensor acquisition interface logic.
Regulated supply voltage delivered to the ESP32 processing core hosting the control, processing, noise, storage, telemetry, and UI subsystems.
Buffer management directives (flush, clear, overflow policy) issued by the control subsystem to the data buffer and storage subsystem.
Sensor fault events and data-ready status signals reported from the acquisition interface to the control subsystem for state-machine transitions.

assumptions.statement: The ESP32 is the processing and communication platform, as explicitly stated by the user.
The MPU6050 is the inertial measurement unit, as explicitly stated by the user.
The 0.10 g accel_x RMS noise threshold is a hard pass/fail criterion applied during stationary conditions.
Acceleration telemetry streaming is a primary continuous function of the device, not a one-time or on-demand operation.
The telemetry transport medium and destination host have not been specified; the architecture treats the transport as an abstract communication interface.
Whether noise verification operates as a one-time factory/calibration step or as a continuous runtime health check has not been determined; the architecture supports both modes.
The sampling rate and data resolution for the inertial sensor have not been specified; these are treated as configurable parameters within the sensor's supported range.
Axes beyond accel_x (accel_y, accel_z, gyroscope channels) are treated as optionally in scope; the architecture accommodates them without mandating their inclusion.
A stationary-condition detection gate (e.g., low variance or external trigger) is required to ensure noise analysis windows are valid; the specific criterion is unresolved.
The power source type (battery, USB, regulated bench supply) and power budget have not been specified; the power management subsystem is designed to be source-agnostic.
A local status and diagnostic interface is included to support field verification of noise threshold compliance, even though no explicit UI requirement was stated.
